translations.structuredDataDisambiguatingDescription: Developer with a focus on security
translations.bookHackersMindSummary: Bruce Schneier impressively shows which sometimes dangerous dependencies have developed over the past decades between the world of computers and our social, economic and political systems.
translations.bookWebApplicationSecuritySummary: Andrew Hoffman divides application security into three pillars and presents current attacks and countermeasures as part of a secure development process.
translations.bookCountdownToZeroDaySummary: Kim Zetter tells the gripping story of a virus that sabotaged Iran's nuclear programme and opens up a view of a new era of digital warfare in which digital attacks can cause unimagined destruction.
translations.bookAngularSummary: With this book, the authors have managed to explain both beginner and more advanced concepts clearly and understandably. The theoretical aspects are illustrated with very good examples.
translations.vitaSecurityTitle: Head of Application Security Task Force
translations.vitaSecurityDescription: Alongside my personal passion for solving CTFs on platforms such as Hack The Box and ongoing professional training in security topics, I lead the Application Security Task Force. Its goal is the <mark>continuous improvement of the security</mark> of existing and new applications developed and operated within the group. The task force's work focuses, among other things, on supporting <mark>penetration tests</mark>, evaluating the security of a wide range of <mark>system and software architectures</mark> and shaping <mark>secure coding practices</mark>.
translations.vitaDeveloperDescription: As a full-stack developer, I focus on working with <mark>Java, Node.js</mark> and various web technologies such as <mark>TypeScript, JavaScript and PHP</mark>. In this context, I work with the content management system <mark>FirstSpirit</mark> and the portal software <mark>Liferay</mark>. Within these two system environments, I maintain a large number of central websites and web applications of the MERKUR GROUP (formerly Gauselmann Group). In addition, I developed a <mark>platform for managing, planning and carrying out rollout processes</mark> using modern frameworks such as <mark>Angular</mark> and <mark>NestJS</mark>.
translations.vitaBachelorTitle: Dual Study Programme - Bachelor of Science (B.Sc.)
translations.vitaBachelorDescription:
During my studies in business information systems, I worked intensively on practical projects in several modules alongside many theoretical aspects. These included programming a prototype iOS app with a backend for controlling a DJI drone for automated warehouse management, developing a chatbot and programming an Alexa skill. These projects allowed me to apply the knowledge I had learned in theory and, often as part of a team, to develop innovative solutions. In the later semesters, I chose to specialise in e-business.
My bachelor's thesis covered the concept, design and Java implementation of an extension for a content management system.
translations.vitaApprenticeshipTitle: Dual Study Programme - IT Specialist for System Integration (FiSi)
translations.vitaApprenticeshipDescription:
As part of my dual study programme at the MERKUR GROUP (formerly Gauselmann Group), I completed vocational training as an IT specialist for system integration. After each theory phase at the university, I moved to a different department within the company. This gave me a wide range of insights into both administrative tasks and software development processes. Along the way, I gained experience with databases, virtualisation technologies and custom software development, among other things.
In my final project, I designed and implemented a solution for end-to-end monitoring of email infrastructures.
translations.vitaSchoolDescription: Even at school I discovered my passion for computer science, which grew out of an <mark>elective computer science course</mark> in middle school and was strengthened further by an <mark>internship in automation engineering</mark>. Besides regular school life, I also worked as an administrator in the school's self-study centre, which gave me my first valuable practical experience back then. In my final years, I took <mark>advanced courses in mathematics and social sciences</mark>. In particular, the combination of my interest in numbers and logic and my understanding of economic relationships led me to decide on studying business information systems while I was still at school.
